title: Feature Engineering
text:
Preliminaries
In this chapter we shall construct micro-level and mezo-level variables with respect to time, spatial, and other dimensions. Optional Tourism indicating the severity of restrictions during COVID will be included also.
Our Tourism is already in long format, that is, every accommodation establishment is represented by several rows and each row covers Tourism for one month. Such format is convenient in terms of constructing new variables, especially statistics taking into account time dimension.

title: Feature Engineering
text:
Feature construction
The model we aim to developed is general, that is, we do not aim to model a particular month, e.g. June, but to model variable \(Y_t\) at time point \(t\) based on previous monthly Tourism \(Y_{t-1}\), \(Y_{t-2}\) at points \(t-1\), \(t-2\), etc. To this end, lagged target variable need to be constructed. Within feature construction stage, utilizing lagged target variable, NUTS identifiers, type of accommodation establishment, information about COVID-19 restriction, many variables may be constructed. For time window of 3, 6 and 12 months, several statistics shall be calculated, namely:

mean,
median,
the first quartile,
the third quartile,
sum,

with respect to NUTS identifiers, type of accommodation establishment. Also lags of order 1, 2 and 3 of target variable shall be included.

Auxiliary functions
To make the process more transparent we break it down into several steps and each step is implemented with soem auxiliary function. The first function ASSIGN_LAG creates a lag for a given column by one period. The assignment is based on the provided key variable.

ASSIGN_LAG <- function(source_Tourism, Tourism_to_assign = "tourists", lag_n = 1) 
{
  
  matching_cols <- c(
    "regon",
    "voivodeship",
    "county",
    "object_type",
    "is_seasonal"
  )
  
  stopifnot(Tourism_to_assign %in% names(source_Tourism))
  
  source_Tourism %>%
    mutate(
      month = str_pad(month, 2, pad = "0"),
      .period_sort = if ("period_yyyymm" %in% names(.)) {
        as.integer(period_yyyymm)
      } else {
        as.integer(paste0(year, month))
      }
    ) %>%
    arrange(
      across(all_of(matching_cols)),
      .period_sort
    ) %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(matching_cols))) %>%
    mutate(
      !!paste0(Tourism_to_assign, "_minus", lag_n) :=
        dplyr::lag(.data[[Tourism_to_assign]], lag_n)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(-.period_sort)
}

Based on that, the function ASSIGN_MULTIPLE_LAGS automatically creates multiple backward lags (the number of periods is determined by lags).

ASSIGN_MULTIPLE_LAGS <- function(source_Tourism, Tourism_to_assign = "tourists", lags = 1:3) 
{
  result <- source_Tourism
  for (lag_n in lags) 
    {
    result <- ASSIGN_LAG(result, Tourism_to_assign = Tourism_to_assign, lag_n = lag_n)
    }
  result
}

The following functions will generate statistics based on lagged variables.

add_rolling_windows <- function(Tourism,
                                variable = "tourists",
                                windows = c(3, 6, 12),
                                stats = c("mean", "median"),
                                group_by_cols = c("voivodeship", "county", "object_type"))
{
  
  stat_funs <- list(
    mean   = function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = function(x) median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25    = function(x) quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75    = function(x) quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum    = function(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  
  if (!all(stats %in% names(stat_funs))) {
    stop("Some requested statistics are not defined in 'stat_funs'")
  }
  
  Tourism %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(group_by_cols))) %>%
    group_modify(~ {
      
      df <- .x %>% arrange(year, month)
      
      lagged_var <- dplyr::lag(df[[variable]])
      
      for (stat_name in stats) {
        for (w in windows) {
          
          col_name <- paste0(
            stat_name, "_win_", w, "_by_",
            paste(group_by_cols, collapse = "_")
          )
          
          df[[col_name]] <- zoo::rollapply(
            lagged_var,                 # <-- używamy opóźnionej zmiennej
            width = w,
            FUN = stat_funs[[stat_name]],
            align = "right",
            partial = TRUE,
            fill = NA
          )
        }
      }
      
      df
    }) %>%
    ungroup()
}


# Adding the share within the county and the voivodeship

calculate_share <- function(Tourism, variable = "tourists", windows = c(3, 6, 12),
                            group_share = c("county", "voivodeship")) 
{
  
  # unique identifier 
  Tourism <- Tourism %>%
    mutate(county_uniq = paste0(voivodeship, "_", county))
  
  result <- Tourism
  
  for (grp in group_share) {
    
    # if calculating share relative to county, use county_uniq
    if (grp == "county") {
      group_var <- "county_uniq"
    } else {
      group_var <- grp
    }
    
    for (w in windows) {
      
      col_name <- paste0("share_", w, "mo_vs_", grp)
      
      result <- result %>%
        group_by(across(all_of(group_var))) %>%
        arrange(year, month, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
        mutate(
          tmp_sum = zoo::rollapply(
            .data[[variable]],
            width = w,
            FUN = sum,
            align = "right",
            partial = TRUE,
            fill = NA
          )
        ) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        mutate(!!col_name := .data[[variable]] / tmp_sum) %>%
        select(-tmp_sum)
    }
  }
  
  result %>% select(-county_uniq)
}

Feature construction in action
It is time to execute all function developed for feature construction. First, generate lagged target variable

Tourism <- ASSIGN_MULTIPLE_LAGS(Tourism, Tourism_to_assign = "tourists", lags = 1:3)
Rolling means for specific windows and groups
Tourism <- add_rolling_windows(
  Tourism = Tourism,
  variable = "tourists",
  windows = c(3, 6, 12),
  stats = c("mean"),
  group_by_cols = c("regon", "object_type")
)
Rolling means, medians, and quartiles for object_type
Tourism <- add_rolling_windows(
  Tourism = Tourism,
  variable = "tourists",
  windows = c(3, 6, 12),
  stats = c("mean", "median", "q25", "q75"),
  group_by_cols = "object_type"
)
Rolling stats for multiple grouping variables
Tourism <- add_rolling_windows(
  Tourism = Tourism,
  variable = "tourists",
  windows = c(3, 6, 12),
  stats = c("mean", "median", "q25", "q75"),
  group_by_cols = c("voivodeship", "county", "object_type")
)
Rolling sums for regional totals
Tourism <- add_rolling_windows(
  Tourism = Tourism,
  variable = "tourists",
  windows = c(3, 6, 12),
  stats = c("sum"),
  group_by_cols = c("regon", "voivodeship", "county")
)
Share of tourists per hotel relative to county or voivodeship
Tourism <- calculate_share(
  Tourism = Tourism,
  variable = "tourists",
  windows = c(3, 6, 12),
  group_share = c("county", "voivodeship")
)

title: Early imputation in the Polish survey of accommodation establishments
text:
About dataset
Statistics Poland conducts a survey of accommodation establishments with 10 or more bed-places:

Mandatory survey on monthly base.
Census survey of approx. 15 ths. of establishments.
The deadline for submitting reports is the 10th day after the reporting month. In practice, establishments report throughout the entire month.
Unit response rate is approximately 80% and varies due to seasonality.
Item non-response pertains mostly to foreign tourist data.

The survey covers tourist accommodation establishments regardless of the type, owner, and location, as well as establishments with other purposes (not related to tourism) that are temporarily used by tourists (e.g., student dormitories, sports and recreation centers).
Tourist accommodation establishments classified into the following activity groups according to NACE Rev. 2 classification:

55.1 – hotels and similar accommodation,
55.2 – holiday and other short-stay accommodation,
55.3 – camping grounds, recreational vehicle parks and trailer parks.

The study covers 20 types of tourist accommodation establishments. Data is collected with “Report on the occupancy of tourist accommodation establishments”:


Problem statement
Due to variety of booking systems, accommodation establishments report their data with different timeliness. In such case, early imputation can be used for flash estimates of statistics of accommodation establishments.




ReuseCC-BY 4.0

These variables are interpreted as follows:

regon - ID of accommodation establishment (original Polish name of ID but content is completely different)
voivodeship - administrative region code (closely corresponds to NUTS 2)
county - administrative region code (former LAU 2)
object_type - recoded type of accommodation establishments, e.g. hotel, motel, etc.
is_seasonal - 1 when operates through whole year, 2 - when operates in a part of a year (e.g. in a summer or in a winter season)
period_yyyymm - text label of year and month of reporting (convenient for Tourism ordering)
tourists - number of tourists accommodated (variable of interest)
month_num - number of month (1 for January)
active_in_month - 1 when establishment operated in a given month (there are many cases when establishment does not provide number of tourists but declares it was active)
year - year as integer
month - text label of the month

Some additional variables will make further analysis more convenient.

  geom_histogram(bins = 80, fill = "#2C3E50", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log10", labels = label_comma()) +  
  labs(
    title = "Histogram of Tourists (Logarithmic Scale)",
    x = "Number of Tourists (log10)",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)








It turns out that the distribution of monthly number of tourist is close to log-normal.
The following plot reveals trend and seasonality of total number of tourists and pandemic effect.

tot_month <- Tourism %>%
  group_by(period_date) %>%
  summarise(total_tourists = sum(tourists, na.rm=TRUE))

ggplot(tot_month, aes(x = period_date, y = total_tourists/1000)) +
  geom_line(aes(col=total_tourists/1000)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = '6 months')+
  scale_color_viridis_c()+
  labs(title = "", x = "Month", y = "Total number of tourists [ths.]")+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = 'none')








Autumn and winter season during pandemic resulted in large decrease. Summer period was without severe restrictions and the number of tourists increased but not to pre-pandemic level. The pandemic situation has a heterogeneous effect in regional breakdown (voivodeships).

top_voiv <- Tourism %>%
  count(voivodeship, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 16) %>%
  pull(voivodeship)

Tourism %>% filter(voivodeship %in% top_voiv) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = period_date, y = tourists, color = voivodeship, group = voivodeship)) +
  stat_summary(geom = "line", fun = mean, size = 1) +
  stat_summary(geom = "point", fun = mean, size = 2) +  
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Average number of tourists",
    color = "Voivodeship"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~voivodeship)+
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),legend.position = 'none')

regon - ID of accommodation establishment (original Polish name of ID but content is completely different)
voivodeship - administrative region code (closely corresponds to NUTS 2)
county - administrative region code (former LAU 2)
object_type - recoded type of accommodation establishments, e.g. hotel, motel, etc.
is_seasonal - 1 when operates through whole year, 2 - when operates in a part of a year (e.g. in a summer or in a winter season)
period_yyyymm - text label of year and month of reporting (convenient for Tourism ordering)
tourists - number of tourists accommodated (variable of interest)
month_num - number of month (1 for January)
active_in_month - 1 when establishment operated in a given month (there are many cases when establishment does not provide number of tourists but declares it was active)
year - year as integer
month - text label of the month

Some additional variables will make further analysis more convenient.

title: Explanatory Tourism Analysis
text:
In this section we explore our Tourism through several plots. First, we start with histogram but on log scale.

library(scales)


Attaching package: 'scales'


The following object is masked from 'package:purrr':

    discard


The following object is masked from 'package:readr':

    col_factor

Tourism %>% filter(tourists>0) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = tourists)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 80, fill = "#2C3E50", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log10", labels = label_comma()) +  
  labs(
    title = "Histogram of Tourists (Logarithmic Scale)",
    x = "Number of Tourists (log10)",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)








It turns out that the distribution of monthly number of tourist is close to log-normal.
The following plot reveals trend and seasonality of total number of tourists and pandemic effect.

tot_month <- Tourism %>%
  group_by(period_date) %>%
  summarise(total_tourists = sum(tourists, na.rm=TRUE))

ggplot(tot_month, aes(x = period_date, y = total_tourists/1000)) +
  geom_line(aes(col=total_tourists/1000)) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = '6 months')+
  scale_color_viridis_c()+
  labs(title = "", x = "Month", y = "Total number of tourists [ths.]")+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = 'none')








Autumn and winter season during pandemic resulted in large decrease. Summer period was without severe restrictions and the number of tourists increased but not to pre-pandemic level. The pandemic situation has a heterogeneous effect in regional breakdown (voivodeships).

top_voiv <- Tourism %>%
  count(voivodeship, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 16) %>%
  pull(voivodeship)

Tourism %>% filter(voivodeship %in% top_voiv) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = period_date, y = tourists, color = voivodeship, group = voivodeship)) +
  stat_summary(geom = "line", fun = mean, size = 1) +
  stat_summary(geom = "point", fun = mean, size = 2) +  
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Average number of tourists",
    color = "Voivodeship"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~voivodeship)+
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),legend.position = 'none')

title: Explanatory Tourism Analysis
text:
We shall use an old-fashion shape file to create several spatial visualizations.

library(RColorBrewer)
library(gridExtra)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

# URL to ZIP stored in your repo
url <- 'https://github.com/AIML4OS/WP9_S1_PL_TOURISM/raw/refs/heads/main/sspcloud/voivodeships.zip'

# download into temporary file
zip_temp <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
download.file(url, zip_temp, mode = "wb")

# unpack temporary file
temp_dir <- tempdir()
unzip(zip_temp, exdir = temp_dir)

# find shape file
shp_file <- list.files(temp_dir, pattern = "\\.shp$", full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)

# load
poland_map <- st_read(shp_file)

Prepare keys for merging.

voivodeship_names <- c(

  "32"="Zachodniopomorskie"
) %>% tolower()

tur_year <- tur_year %>%
  mutate(voivodeship_name = voivodeship_names[voivodeship])

Time for choropleth.

  map_df <- poland_map %>%
    left_join(filter(tur_year, year == "2019"), by = c("JPT_NAZWA_" = "voivodeship_name"))
  ggplot(map_df) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = tourists/1000), color = "white") +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colors = brewer.pal(9, "Blues"),
                        na.value = "grey90",
                        labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(title = paste("Year", "2019"), fill = "Tourists [ths.]") +
    theme_minimal()








Most of tourist visit Małpolskie voivodeship, and then Mazowiecki voivodeship - capital region. Seaside region are also popular.
